text:
Let $S=\left \{x\in [-6,3]-\{-2,2\}:\frac{|x+3|-1}{|x|-2}\geq 0\right \}$ and $T=\left \{x\in \mathrm{ℤ}:x^{2}-7|x|+9\leq 0\right \}$.

Then the number of elements in $\mathrm{S}\cap \mathrm{T}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $T$: $x^{2}=|x|^{2}$, so $|x|^{2}-7|x|+9\leq 0$. The roots of $u^{2}-7u+9=0$ are $u=\dfrac{7\pm \sqrt{13}}{2}\approx 1.70,5.30$, so

$\frac{7-\sqrt{13}}{2}\leq |x|\leq \frac{7+\sqrt{13}}{2}\Rightarrow |x|\in \{2,3,4,5\}$

$T=\{\pm 2,\pm 3,\pm 4,\pm 5\}$.

$S$ allows only $x\in [-6,3]$ with $x\neq \pm 2$, and $4,5$ lie outside $[-6,3]$, so the elements of $T$ to test are $-5,-4,-3,3$.

$x=3$: $\dfrac{6-1}{3-2}=5\geq 0$, so $3\in S$.

$x=-3$: $\dfrac{0-1}{3-2}=-1<0$, so $-3\notin S$.

$x=-4$: $\dfrac{1-1}{4-2}=0\geq 0$, so $-4\in S$.

$x=-5$: $\dfrac{2-1}{5-2}=\dfrac{1}{3}\geq 0$, so $-5\in S$.

So $S\cap T=\{-5,-4,3\}$, which has 3 elements.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text: Let $α$, $β$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2}-\sqrt{2}x+\sqrt{6}=0$ and $\frac{1}{α^{2}}+1,\frac{1}{β^{2}}+1$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2}+ax+b=0$. Then the roots of the equation $x^{2}-(a+b-2)x+(a+b+2)=0$ are :
options: real and exactly one of them is positive
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$α+β=\sqrt{2}$, $αβ=\sqrt{6}$

$\frac{1}{α^{2}}+1+\frac{1}{β^{2}}+1=2+\frac{α^{2}+β^{2}}{6}$

$=2+\frac{2-2\sqrt{6}}{6}=-a$

$\left (\frac{1}{α^{2}}+1\right )\left (\frac{1}{β^{2}}+1\right )=1+\frac{1}{α^{2}}+\frac{1}{β^{2}}+\frac{1}{α^{2}β^{2}}$

$=\frac{7}{6}+\frac{2-2\sqrt{6}}{6}=b$

$\Rightarrow a+b=\frac{-5}{6}$

So, equation is $x^{2}+\frac{17x}{6}+\frac{7}{6}=0$

OR $6x^{2}+17x+7=0$

Both roots of equation are $-$ve and distinct

text: Let $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ be any two $3\times 3$ symmetric and skew symmetric matrices respectively. Then which of the following is NOT true?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $A^{T}=A$ and $B^{T}=-B$, so $(A^{n})^{T}=A^{n}$ and $(B^{n})^{T}=(-B)^{n}=(-1)^{n}B^{n}$.

(A): $(A^{4}-B^{4})^{T}=A^{4}-B^{4}$, so $A^{4}-B^{4}$ is symmetric (true).

(B): $(AB-BA)^{T}=B^{T}A^{T}-A^{T}B^{T}=-BA+AB=AB-BA$, so $AB-BA$ is symmetric (true).

(D): $(AB+BA)^{T}=B^{T}A^{T}+A^{T}B^{T}=-BA-AB=-(AB+BA)$, so $AB+BA$ is skew-symmetric (true).

(C): $(B^{5}-A^{5})^{T}=-B^{5}-A^{5}$, while $-(B^{5}-A^{5})=-B^{5}+A^{5}$. These are equal only when $A^{5}=O$; for $A=I$ they differ, so $B^{5}-A^{5}$ is not skew-symmetric in general (not true).

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text:
The function $f:\mathrm{ℝ}\to \mathrm{ℝ}$ defined by 

$f(x)=\lim _{n\to \infty }\frac{\cos (2πx)-x^{2n}\sin (x-1)}{1+x^{2n+1}-x^{2n}}$ is continuous for all x in :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $|x|<1$, $x^{2n}\to 0$ and $x^{2n+1}\to 0$, so $f(x)=\cos 2πx$.

For $|x|>1$, dividing numerator and denominator by $x^{2n}$:

$f(x)=\lim _{n\to \infty }\frac{\dfrac{\cos 2πx}{x^{2n}}-\sin (x-1)}{\dfrac{1}{x^{2n}}+x-1}=-\frac{\sin (x-1)}{x-1}$

At $x=1$: $f(1)=\dfrac{\cos 2π-\sin 0}{1+1-1}=1$. At $x=-1$: $f(-1)=\dfrac{\cos 2π-\sin (-2)}{1-1-1}=-(1+\sin 2)$.

At $x=1$: $\lim _{x\to 1^{-}}f(x)=\cos 2π=1$ and $\lim _{x\to 1^{+}}f(x)=-\lim _{x\to 1^{+}}\dfrac{\sin (x-1)}{x-1}=-1$, so $f$ is discontinuous at $x=1$.

At $x=-1$: $\lim _{x\to -1^{+}}f(x)=\cos (-2π)=1$ and $\lim _{x\to -1^{-}}f(x)=-\dfrac{\sin (-2)}{-2}=-\dfrac{\sin 2}{2}$, so $f$ is discontinuous at $x=-1$.

Both $\cos 2πx$ and $-\dfrac{\sin (x-1)}{x-1}$ are continuous on their intervals, so $f$ is continuous on $\mathrm{ℝ}-\{-1,1\}$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text: The sum of the absolute maximum and absolute minimum values of the function $f(x)=\tan ^{-1}(\sin x-\cos x)$ in the interval $[0,π]$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$g(x)=\sin x-\cos x=\sqrt{2}\sin \left (x-\dfrac{π}{4}\right )$. For $x\in [0,π]$, $x-\dfrac{π}{4}\in \left [-\dfrac{π}{4},\dfrac{3π}{4}\right ]$, so $\sin \left (x-\dfrac{π}{4}\right )\in \left [-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}},1\right ]$ and $g(x)\in [-1,\sqrt{2}]$, with $-1$ at $x=0$ and $\sqrt{2}$ at $x=\dfrac{3π}{4}$.

Since $\tan ^{-1}$ is increasing, $f_{\min }=\tan ^{-1}(-1)=-\dfrac{π}{4}$ and $f_{\max }=\tan ^{-1}\sqrt{2}$.

For $θ=\tan ^{-1}\sqrt{2}\in \left (0,\dfrac{π}{2}\right )$, $\cos θ=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+\tan ^{2}θ}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, so $\tan ^{-1}\sqrt{2}=\cos ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )$.

$f_{\max }+f_{\min }=\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )-\frac{π}{4}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

solution.body:
By the fundamental theorem of calculus, $I_{n}^{'}(x)=\dfrac{1}{(x^{2}+5)^{n}}$.

Integrating $I_{n}$ by parts, with $\dfrac{1}{(t^{2}+5)^{n}}$ as the first function and $1$ as the second:

$I_{n}(x)=\left [\frac{t}{(t^{2}+5)^{n}}\right ]_{0}^{x}+2n\int\limits _{0}^{x}\frac{t^{2}}{(t^{2}+5)^{n+1}}dt$

Writing $t^{2}=(t^{2}+5)-5$ in the last integral:

$\int\limits _{0}^{x}\frac{t^{2}}{(t^{2}+5)^{n+1}}dt=I_{n}(x)-5I_{n+1}(x)$

So

$I_{n}=\frac{x}{(x^{2}+5)^{n}}+2nI_{n}-10nI_{n+1}\Rightarrow 10nI_{n+1}-(2n-1)I_{n}=\frac{x}{(x^{2}+5)^{n}}=xI_{n}^{'}(x)$

For $n=5$:

$50I_{6}-9I_{5}=xI_{5}^{'}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

solution.body:
[IMG]


According to NTA, the required region $A_{2}$ which is shaded in crossed lines and comes out to be

$A_{2}=\int\limits _{1}^{2}\left (\ln \frac{2}{y}-e^{y}+e^{2}\right )dy=1+e-\ln 2$

But according to us the required region $A_{1}$ comes out to be shaded in parallel lines, which can be obtained as

$\begin{array}{ll} A_{1} & =\int\limits _{0}^{\ln 2}\left (\ln \left (x+e^{2}\right )-2e^{-x}\right )dx \\  \\ =\left \{\left (x+e^{2}\right )\ln \left (x+e^{2}\right )-x+2e^{-x}\right \}\left |_{0}^{\ln 2} \\  \\ =\left (\ln 2+e^{2}\right )\ln \left (\ln 2+e^{2}\right )-\ln 2+1 \\  \\ -2e^{2}-2 \\  \\ =\left (\ln 2+e^{2}\right )\ln \left (\ln 2+e^{2}\right )-\ln 2-2e^{2}-1 \end{array} \right.$

Not given in any option.

The region asked in the question is bounded by three curves

$\begin{array}{l} y=\ln \left (x+e^{2}\right ) \\  \\ x=\ln \left (\dfrac{2}{y}\right ) \\  \\ x=\ln 2 \end{array}$

There is only one region which satisfies above requirement and which also lies above line $y=1$

 Line $y=1$ may or may not be the boundary of the region.

text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{1}{x^{2}-1}y=\left (\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right )^{1/2}$, $x>1$  passing through the point $\left (2,\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}}\right )$. Then $\sqrt{7}y(8)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{1}{x^{2}-1}y=\sqrt{\frac{x-1}{x+1}},x>1$

Integrating factor I.F. $=e^{\int \frac{1}{x2-1}dx}=e^{\frac{1}{2}\ln \left |\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right |}$

$=\sqrt{\frac{x-1}{x+1}}$

Solution of differential equation

$y\sqrt{\frac{x-1}{x+1}}=\int \frac{x-1}{x+1}dx=\int \left (1-\frac{2}{x+1}\right )dx$

$y\sqrt{\frac{x-1}{x+1}}=x-2\ln |x+1|+C$

Curve passes through $\left (2,\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}}\right )$

$\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=2-2\ln 3+C$

$C=2\ln 3-\frac{5}{3}$

$y(8)\times \frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}=8-2\ln 9+2\ln 3-\frac{5}{3}$

$\sqrt{7}.y(8)=19-6\ln 3$

text: Let the hyperbola $H:\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ pass through the point $(2\sqrt{2},-2\sqrt{2})$. A parabola is drawn whose focus is same as the focus of $\mathrm{H}$ with positive abscissa and the directrix of the parabola passes through the other focus of $\mathrm{H}$. If the length of the latus rectum of the parabola is e times the length of the latus rectum of $\mathrm{H}$, where e is the eccentricity of H, then which of the following points lies on the parabola?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$H:\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$

Focus of parabola : $(ae,0)$

Directrix : $x=-ae$.

Equation of parabola $\equiv y^{2}=4aex$

Length of latus rectum of parabola $=4ae$

Length of latus rectum of hyperbola $=\frac{2.b^{2}}{a}$

as given, $4ae=\frac{2b^{2}}{a}.e$

$2=\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}$ ...... (i)

$\because$ H passes through $\left (2\sqrt{2},-2\sqrt{2}\right )\Rightarrow \frac{8}{a^{2}}-\frac{8}{b^{2}}=1$ ........ (ii)

From (i) and (ii) $a^{2}=4$ and $b^{2}=8\Rightarrow e=\sqrt{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ Equation of parabola is $y^{2}=8\sqrt{3}x$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text: Let the coefficients of the middle terms in the expansion of $\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}+βx\right )^{4},(1-3βx)^{2}$ and $\left (1-\frac{β}{2}x\right )^{6},β>0$, respectively form the first three terms of an A.P. If d is the common difference of this A.P. , then $50-\frac{2d}{β^{2}}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Coefficients of middle terms of given expansions are ${}^{4}C_{2}\frac{1}{6}β^{2},{}^{2}C_{1}(-3β),{}^{6}C_{3}\left (\frac{-β}{2}\right )^{3}$ form an A.P.

$\therefore$ $2.2(-3β)=β^{2}-\frac{5β^{3}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow -24=2β-5β^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 5β^{2}-2β-24=0$

$\Rightarrow 5β^{2}-12β+10β-24=0$

$\Rightarrow β(5β-12)+2(5β-12)=0$

$β=\frac{12}{5}$

$d=-6β-β^{2}$

$\therefore$ $50-\frac{2d}{β^{2}}=50-2\frac{(-6β-β^{2})}{β^{2}}=50+\frac{12}{β}+2=57$

text: Let $\mathrm{z}=a+ib,b\neq 0$ be complex numbers satisfying $z^{2}=\bar{z}\cdot 2^{1-|z|}$. Then the least  value of $n\in N$, such that $z^{n}=(z+1)^{n}$, is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ $z^{2}=z–.2^{1-|z|}$ ...... (1)

$\Rightarrow |z|^{2}=|z–|.2^{1-|z|}$

$\Rightarrow |z|=2^{1-|z|}$,

$\because$ $b\neq 0\Rightarrow |z|\neq 0$

$\therefore$ $|z|=1$ ...... (2)

$\because$ $z=a+ib$ then $\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}=1$ ...... (3)

Now again from equation (1), equation (2), equation (3) we get :

$a^{2}-b^{2}+i2ab=(a-ib)2^{0}$

$\therefore$ $a^{2}-b^{2}=a$ and $2ab=-b$

$\therefore$ $a=-\frac{1}{2}$ and $b=\pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$z=-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i$ or $z=-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i$

$z^{n}=(z+1)^{n}\Rightarrow \left (\frac{z+1}{z}\right )^{n}=1$

$\left (1+\frac{1}{z}\right )^{n}=1$

$\left (\frac{1+\sqrt{3}i}{2}\right )^{n}=1$, then minimum value of n is 6.

text: The value of the integral $\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}60\frac{\sin (6x)}{\sin x}dx$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}60\quad .\frac{\sin 6x}{\sin x}dx$

$=60\qquad .2\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}(3-4\sin ^{2}x)(4\cos ^{2}x-3)\cos xdx$

$=120\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}(3-4\sin ^{2}x)(1-4\sin ^{2}x)\cos xdx$

Let $\sin x=t\Rightarrow \cos xdx=dt$

$=120\int\limits _{0}^{1}(3-4t^{2})(1-4t^{2})dt$

$=120\int\limits _{0}^{1}(3-16t^{2}+16t^{4})dt$

$=120\left [3t-\frac{16t^{3}}{3}+\frac{16t^{5}}{5}\right ]_{0}^{1}$

$=104$
